mainTopic: End of the משנה about conditional vows between husband and wife, and the start of the גמרא: Does new growth from a planted forbidden onion (שביעית or תרומה) cancel the forbidden original?
overview: The amud opens with the last lines of the משנה about a husband whose vow forbids his wife from benefiting from him if she visits her father's house, and how the timing of the condition works. The גמרא then quotes the next משנה ("קונם מעשה ידיך עלי") and brings a question raised by ישמעאל איש כפר ימא. An onion was uprooted in שביעית and replanted in the eighth year, and the permitted new growth became bigger than the forbidden original. Does the new growth cancel the prohibition? רבי יצחק נפחא proves that it does from רבי ינאי's ruling about a planted תרומה onion. רבי ירמיה (or רבי זריקא) objects that two sages rule the other way: רבי יוחנן on a young ערלה vine grafted onto an old vine, and רבי יונתן on an onion planted in a vineyard. רבי אמי then brings a proof from a replanted pound of tithed onions, which must be tithed on the whole crop. The גמרא rejects this proof because that ruling is a stringency. It begins a new proof from a ברייתא of רבי שמעון, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the previous case: going after פסח violates בל יחל
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its earlier case. If the condition is fulfilled after פסח, she has violated בל יחל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she went after פסח, she is liable for violating "He shall not break his word."
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the משנה in the middle. It is finishing a case where she benefited from her husband before פסח and then went to her father's house after פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vow was conditional. Once she goes, the condition is fulfilled, and the benefit she already took is treated as breaking the vow after the fact. That is why she is liable for בל יחל.

keyTerms.meaning: "He shall not profane his word": the prohibition against breaking a vow
Passover; here it marks the time limit of the condition

phrases.english: If she went after Pesach —
she is liable for "He shall not profane."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a משנה case that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the condition of a vow is fulfilled, benefit taken earlier counts as a violation of בל יחל.

steps.title: The reversed case: forbidden until the Festival if she goes before פסח
steps.stepSummary: The husband forbids benefit until the חג if she visits her father before פסח. If she went before פסח, she is forbidden until the חג, but visiting after פסח is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said: "Benefit from me is forbidden to you until the Festival if you go to your father's house before Pesach," and she went before Pesach, she is forbidden to benefit from him until the Festival. She may go after Pesach.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new case where the two time limits are switched. The condition covers the time until פסח, and the ban lasts until the חג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two separate times matter here. One is how long the condition lasts (until פסח). The other is how long the ban lasts (until the חג). Going after פסח is outside the condition, so it triggers nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Benefit (here, benefit that is forbidden by the vow)
The Festival
Benefit from him

steps.whatToRemember: With a conditional vow, check two things: when the condition applies, and how long the ban lasts.

phrases.english: "That you benefit from me until the Festival
phrases.notes: This is vow wording. It means benefit from him is forbidden to her.

phrases.aramaic: אִם הוֹלֶכֶת אַתְּ לְבֵית אָבִיךָ עַד הַפֶּסַח״,
phrases.english: if you go to your father's house until Pesach,"
if she went before Pesach —
she is forbidden to benefit from him until the Festival,
and she is permitted to go after Pesach.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאַתְּ נֶהֱנֵית לִי עַד הֶחָג אִם הוֹלֶכֶת אַתְּ לְבֵית אָבִיךָ עַד הַפֶּסַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reverse case to the one that just ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Going before פסח triggers a ban until the חג. Going after פסח falls outside the condition and is allowed.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the next משנה about "קונם מעשה ידיך"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by quoting the משנה about a husband who forbids his wife's handiwork to himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: One who says to his wife, "Your handiwork is קונם upon me," or "they are קונם upon my mouth," or "they are קונם to my mouth," etc.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה to open its discussion, and the next step brings a question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Quoting the משנה like this shows which line the גמרא is now discussing. Nothing new is ruled here.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows and analyzes the משנה
A vow word that makes something forbidden like a קרבן
Your handiwork: what the wife produces with her hands

phrases.english: Gemara:
One who says to his wife:
"Your handiwork is konam upon me,"
"they are konam upon my mouth,"
"they are konam to my mouth," etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹמֵר לְאִשְׁתּוֹ קֻוֽנָּם מַעֲשֵׂה יָדַיִךְ עָלַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the end of one משנה to the opening of the גמרא's discussion of the next.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes the משנה text as the starting point of the discussion.

steps.title: ישמעאל's question: does new eighth-year growth cancel a שביעית onion?
steps.stepSummary: ישמעאל איש כפר ימא asks about a שביעית onion replanted in the eighth year that grew larger than its original. Do the permitted growths cancel the forbidden original? רבי אמי had no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: ישמעאל איש כפר ימא (some say כפר דימא) asked about an onion uprooted in שביעית and planted in the eighth year, whose new growth became more than the original. The new growth is permitted and the original is forbidden. Since the growth is now bigger, does it cancel the prohibition or not? He asked רבי אמי, who did not have an answer.
steps.whatsHappening: A sage raises a real question about mixing permitted and forbidden parts in one onion. The first sage he asks cannot answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, a forbidden item can be cancelled when it is outweighed by permitted material (ביטול). The question is whether this works when both parts are part of the same growing plant. Here the forbidden part is the original core, and the permitted part grew on it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sabbatical (seventh) Year; its produce has special holiness and restrictions
Its growths: the new part that grew after planting
Its original part: the core that was planted
Literally "raise up"; here, cancel a forbidden item by outweighing it
He did not have it in hand: he had no answer

phrases.english: Yishmael, a man of Kefar Yamma,
and some say, a man of Kefar Dimma,
raised a question
about an onion that one uprooted in the Sabbatical Year,
and planted it in the eighth year,
and its growths became more than its original part.
And this is what he was asking:
Its growths are permitted and its original is forbidden;
since its growths became more than its original —

phrases.aramaic: אוֹתָן גִּידּוּלֵי הֶיתֵּר מַעֲלִין אֶת הָאִיסּוּר,
phrases.english: do those permitted growths cancel the prohibition,
or not?
He came before Rabbi Ami,
and he did not have an answer in hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new question into the discussion after the quote of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether permitted growth that outweighs a forbidden original part cancels that part's prohibition.

steps.title: רבי יצחק נפחא answers from רבי ינאי's planted תרומה onion
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא settles the question using רבי ינאי's ruling: a planted onion of תרומה whose growth outweighs the original is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רבי יצחק נפחא, who answered him from what רבי חנינא תריתאה said in the name of רבי ינאי: an onion of תרומה that was planted, whose growths became more than its original, is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: A second sage gives an answer by pointing to a similar case about תרומה. The case of the תרומה onion that was planted is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works by comparison. In both cases a forbidden onion was planted and permitted growth outgrew it. If the growth cancels תרומה, it should also cancel שביעית.

keyTerms.meaning: He resolved it for him
The priest's portion of produce, forbidden to non-כהנים
Permitted

phrases.english: He came before Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha,
who resolved it for him from this,
which Rabbi Chanina of Terita said
that Rabbi Yannai said:
An onion of terumah that one planted,
and its growths became more than its original —
it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question that רבי אמי could not answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, the permitted growth cancels the original, based on רבי ינאי's ruling about a planted תרומה onion.

steps.title: Objection: why follow one opinion against two?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה (or רבי זריקא) objects that רבי יצחק נפחא is following one sage against the view of two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה, and some say רבי זריקא, said to him: Does the Master leave aside two sages and act like one?!
steps.whatsHappening: Someone challenges the answer just given. He is not attacking the logic of the comparison. He says two other sages rule the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is about who to follow. Normally the ruling goes with the majority, so following רבי ינאי alone against two seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaves aside, abandons
Master: a respectful way to address a sage
Two

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to him,
and some say it was Rabbi Zerika:
Does the Master leave aside two
and act according to one?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from רבי ינאי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק נפחא's reliance on רבי ינאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two sages hold that permitted growth does not cancel the original, so one opinion should not outweigh two.

steps.title: Who are the two sages?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which two sages disagree with רבי ינאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the names behind the objection. This sets up the next step, which brings their rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection only works if real sources exist. So the גמרא now asks who these two sages are.

keyTerms.meaning: Who are they?

phrases.english: Who are the two?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the sources behind the objection.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the two sages who rule against רבי ינאי.

steps.title: First of the two: רבי יוחנן on a young ערלה vine grafted onto an old vine
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו in the name of רבי יוחנן: a young vine with fruit, grafted onto an old vine, stays forbidden even if it grew two hundred times more.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a young vine that was grafted onto an old vine, and there were fruits on it, is forbidden even if it added two hundred times as much.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the first of the two sages, רבי יוחנן. His ruling is that permitted new growth does not cancel the forbidden fruit that was already there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the opposite of רבי ינאי's approach. The new permitted growth is large enough to normally cancel ערלה, yet the original forbidden fruit stays forbidden. The next step names the second sage.

keyTerms.meaning: A young vine, still under ערלה
Grafted or entwined it
An old vine, past the ערלה years
Two hundred

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the new growth itself is forbidden. The point is that the fruit that was already on the young vine stays forbidden, even though it is greatly outweighed.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
A young vine that one grafted onto an old vine,
phrases.notes: The young vine is still in its first three years, so its fruit is ערלה and forbidden.

phrases.english: and there were fruits on it,
even though it added two hundred times as much —
phrases.notes: Two hundred times is the amount that normally cancels out ערלה, so this is a strong case for cancelling.

phrases.english: it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers "who are the two" by bringing the first one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן rules that the original forbidden fruit is not cancelled by permitted growth, even two hundred times over.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling supports the objection to רבי יצחק נפחא and sets up the debate over whether growth cancels a forbidden original.

steps.title: The second sage: an onion planted in a vineyard stays forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר רבי נחמני quotes רבי יונתן. An onion planted in a vineyard stays forbidden even after the vineyard is uprooted. This is the second sage who disagrees with רבי ינאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמואל בר רבי נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: If someone planted an onion in a vineyard, and later the vineyard was uprooted, the onion is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering 'who are the two sages?' It brings רבי יונתן as the second sage, alongside רבי יוחנן from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Planting an onion in a vineyard creates כלאי הכרם, a forbidden mix. Once the vineyard is gone, the onion keeps growing in a permitted way, yet רבי יונתן still says it is forbidden. So the new, permitted growth does not cancel the forbidden original, which is the opposite of רבי ינאי.

keyTerms.meaning: An onion
A vineyard
The forbidden mix of food crops planted among grapevines
Was uprooted

steps.whyThisMatters: Now there are two sages, רבי יוחנן and רבי יונתן, against רבי ינאי. This is why רבי ירמיה (some say רבי זריקא) objected that רבי יצחק נפחא was following one opinion against two.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַבִּי נַחְמָנִי
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shmuel bar Rabbi Naḥmani said
Rabbi Yonatan said:
An onion that one planted in a vineyard,
phrases.notes: Planting food crops among grapevines makes a forbidden mix, so the onion starts out forbidden.

phrases.english: and the vineyard was uprooted — it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַבִּי נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 8 by naming the second of the two sages.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second sage who disagrees with רבי ינאי is רבי יונתן. He forbids an onion planted in a vineyard even after the vineyard is uprooted.

steps.title: רבי אמי's proof from a replanted pound of tithed onions
steps.stepSummary: ישמעאל goes back to רבי אמי, who now brings a proof. A pound of onions that was already tithed and then replanted must be tithed on the entire crop. So the growths cancel the original.
steps.simpleTranslation: ישמעאל came back again to רבי אמי, and רבי אמי answered his question from what רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone tithed a pound of onions and then planted them, the crop must be tithed on all of it. So we see that the new growths cancel the original.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי, who had no answer before, now tries to answer ישמעאל's question with a ruling of רבי יוחנן about tithed onions that were replanted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original onions were already tithed, so they should not need tithing again. Yet the whole crop must be tithed, as if the original onions were swallowed up by the larger new growth. רבי אמי reasons that if growths cancel the original here, they should cancel the forbidden שביעית onion too.

keyTerms.meaning: A litra, a measure of weight, roughly a pound
That he made fit to eat, meaning he tithed it
It is tithed (must have מעשר taken)
And he resolved it for him
So we see, apparently
Cancel out, nullify

phrases.english: He then came again before Rabbi Ami
phrases.notes: This is ישמעאל איש כפר ימא coming back to רבי אמי, who couldn't answer him the first time.

phrases.english: and he resolved it for him from this

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yitzḥak said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
A litra of onions that one tithed and then sowed,
is tithed according to all of it.
Apparently, those growths cancel the original.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי וּפְשַׁיט לֵיהּ מִן הָדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the original question from step 4 and offers a new proof that growths cancel the original.
steps.raayaObject: That permitted growths cancel the forbidden original onion.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יצחק in the name of רבי יוחנן: a tithed pound of onions that was replanted is tithed on the whole crop.

steps.title: Maybe growths only cancel when the result is stricter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבי אמי's proof. Perhaps growths cancel the original only when that leads to a stricter ruling, as with tithing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps a case where the result is stricter is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אמי's proof and says it doesn't prove our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the onion-tithing case, saying the growths cancel the original makes things stricter, because you must tithe more. In the שביעית case, saying the growths cancel would make things easier, because the onion becomes permitted. We can't learn a lenient ruling from a case where the law may simply be strict to be careful.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps
In the direction of stringency, being stricter
Is different

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying growths never cancel the original. It is only saying the tithing case can't prove they cancel when that would make something permitted.

phrases.english: Perhaps a case of stringency is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the tithed onions. The question itself still needs an answer, and step 12 brings a new proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof comes from a strict ruling, but the question asks about a lenient one, so the two cases may not be the same.

steps.title: A new proof is introduced from רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: After the first proof is rejected, the גמרא begins to bring a different proof, from a ברייתא quoting רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, prove it from what was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון says:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא drops the rejected proof and introduces a new source, and רבי שמעון's actual words come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא signals that the earlier proof is set aside and a better one is coming. רבי שמעון's ruling itself, which will be used to answer the question, follows right after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the previous approach)
As was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Rather, from this, as it was taught in a baraita,
Rabbi Shimon says:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מִן הָדָא דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof rejected in step 11 with a new source.
steps.raayaObject: Whether permitted growths cancel the forbidden original onion.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי שמעון (its content continues past this line).
